output.brief:
The wrong expiry dates did not come from the agency operators or the printer firmware. The printer job records show that from 4 Oct the data sent to the printers already carried a 36-month shelf life. Nobody overrode it, and the camera only checks print against the job, so it passed every carton. On 3 Oct Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month value for Veltranol that was meant to apply only from 1 Mar 2027, and the 24-month value is still the one in effect. The system nonetheless sent the 36-month value to the line. That conflicts with the vendor's statement that it only uses the value in effect on the job date. Thirty earlier jobs, including some run by agency operators after the firmware change, were correct. Two Veltranol lots on Line 1 day shift are also wrong, in the warehouse.

Next steps:
- Do not warn or remove the agency operators.
- Reset the Veltranol shelf-life records.
- Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two Line 1 lots.
- Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup.
- Check retained cartons of the two other products with future-dated edits (HX-15-30, MR-05-14).
- Ask the vendor why a future-dated value was sent.

I'm fairly confident on cause. Other products are still unchecked.
